reference.method: damped Newton at 50 digits on the README log density, from the fitted values

global.statement: With both coefficients free, every nonempty sample of nonnegative integers has an MLE. The zero probability is the observed zero fraction. If there is a positive observation, the positive-count probability is unique, including $p=0$ when every positive count is one. With all-zero data, $p_0=1$ and $p$ is unidentified. Holding either coefficient leaves the same maximization for the other, provided the held values give positive likelihood. Holding both leaves only likelihood evaluation.
global.reason: The likelihood factors into the Bernoulli likelihood of the zero indicators and a logarithmic-series likelihood for the positive counts. The latter is a one-parameter exponential family with natural parameter $\log p$. Its mean increases strictly from one to infinity because its derivative in that parameter is its positive variance. Strict concavity therefore gives a unique root for a positive-count mean above one. At mean one the maximum is the attained member $p=0$. With no positive counts this factor is absent.
